facts: In Greek myth, Prometheus stole fire from the gods to give it to humanity.
Some Greek stories credit Prometheus with shaping humans from clay.
Prometheus hid stolen fire inside a fennel stalk in Hesiod's account.
Prometheus tricked Zeus with an offering of bones disguised beneath appealing fat.
Prometheus's punishment involved an eagle eating a liver that regrew each night.
Heracles eventually freed Prometheus in a major version of the myth.
Prometheus's name is traditionally interpreted as forethought; Epimetheus's as afterthought.
Mary Shelley's Frankenstein carries the alternative title The Modern Prometheus.
In Hesiod's story, Pandora arrives as part of Zeus's retaliation for Prometheus's deception.
Pandora's famous container was a jar in the ancient account, not a box.
In Greek myth, Ariadne gave Theseus thread to retrace his route through the Labyrinth.
Theseus's father left a sword and sandals beneath a heavy rock as proof of his son's identity.
Young Theseus chose the dangerous land route to Athens rather than the safer sea journey.
In the myth, Aegeus recognised Theseus by his sword before he drank poisoned wine.
Theseus volunteered to accompany the young Athenians sent to Crete's Minotaur.
Theseus forgot to change his ship's black sails, leading his father to believe he had died.
The Aegean Sea's name is linked in myth to King Aegeus.
Ariadne was abandoned on Naxos in a familiar version of Theseus's return voyage.
The ship of Theseus became a philosophical puzzle about identity after all its parts were replaced.
In Greek legend, Theseus captured the bull that had been terrorising Marathon.
Heracles is the Greek hero whom the Romans called Hercules.
Heracles's famous labours were originally ten; two were rejected, bringing the total to twelve.
Heracles cleaned the Augean stables by diverting rivers through them.
Heracles wore the Nemean lion's skin after defeating it.
Iolaus helped Heracles defeat the Hydra by burning its severed neck stumps.
One of Heracles's tasks required capturing Artemis's sacred deer alive.
Heracles frightened the Stymphalian birds into flight with a rattle supplied by Athena.
Heracles had to capture Cerberus, the guardian dog of the underworld.
Heracles joined the Argonauts in stories outside his twelve labours.
Greek stories describe Heracles as both a mortal hero and a figure later admitted among the gods.
Odysseus tricked the Cyclops by claiming his name was Nobody.
In the Odyssey, a bag thought to contain treasure actually held dangerous winds.
Circe transformed some of Odysseus's companions into pigs.
Odysseus returned to Ithaca disguised as a beggar.
Odysseus's old dog Argos recognised him after his long absence.
A nurse recognised Odysseus by a scar from a boar hunt.
Penelope tested Odysseus with a bed built around a living olive tree.
The Odyssey describes a ten-year homeward journey after the Trojan War.
Odysseus won the bow contest that none of Penelope's suitors could complete.
Greek tradition credits Odysseus with devising the Trojan Horse strategy.
In Greek myth, Perseus used a reflection to approach Medusa without meeting her gaze.
The Graeae sisters shared one eye, which Perseus seized to obtain information.
Perseus and his mother survived being cast out to sea inside a chest.
Perseus rescued Andromeda from a sea monster, not from Medusa.
Perseus used a helmet of invisibility to escape the surviving Gorgons.
Even after Medusa's death, her severed head retained its petrifying power in the myth.
Zeus reached Perseus's imprisoned mother in the form of a shower of gold.
Perseus is a legendary founder of Mycenae.
Perseus was both a half-brother and an ancestor of Heracles in Greek genealogies.
A fisherman named Dictys sheltered Perseus and his mother when their chest reached shore.
